title: Iqlab: the noon becomes a hidden meem before baa: rule card and examples
subject: Qur'an & Tajweed
unit: Spring 1: Al-Qadr, Al-'Alaq 1 to 12 and the noon sakinah rules
source: Written for quran/y3 lesson 15 (Pupil PDF worksheet: Iqlab rule card and examples)
intro: Lesson 15. Read the rule and say every example aloud. Point to each word in your mushaf. Then answer the questions.

panels.title: Iqlab: one letter, ب
points: Noon or tanween becomes a meem sound
Lips close gently, hum two counts

head: Not this
This
rows: min ba'd: a clear noon, or a hard 'mm' pressed shut
mim-ba'd: lips touch lightly, two-count hum, then baa

keywords.def: changing the noon into a hidden meem before baa
a humming sound from the nose, held for two counts
the letter م, made with the lips

questions.q: Read «لَيُنۢبَذَنَّ» (104:4). Find the iqlab and say how to read it.
questions.a: Noon sakinah before baa inside the word: layum-badhanna, lips touching, two-count hum.

questions.q: On the pupil PDF, find the iqlab in Al-Humazah (104) and Al-Bayyinah 98:4 and draw the small meem sign above each. Today's rota group recites Al-'Alaq 96:1 to 8 to the teacher in turn.
Extend: write the four rules of noon sakinah with one letter for each.
questions.a: Izhar: ء; idgham: م; iqlab: ب; ikhfa: (week 5) for example ك.

questions.q: Stretch: why do you think the noon turns into meem before baa?
questions.a: Meem and baa are both made with the lips, so a meem sound flows easily into the baa.
A) مِنۢ بَعْدِ. Only baa makes iqlab. مِنْ عَلَقٍ is izhar ('ayn); مِّن كُلِّ is ikhfa (kaaf).

questions.q: The small meem (ۢ) in the mushaf tells us ...
Think again: Try saying 'n' and then 'b' quickly: 'min ba'd'. What do your lips want to do?
questions.a: They close, so the noon turns into a meem sound: iqlab. The mushaf shows a small meem (ۢ) to tell us.
